correctness.rationale: Cartesian distances make each horizontal layer and two-layer prism geodesically convex. The cycle-only dual subset classification is proved directly. Three explicit geodesic obstructions eliminate all but the antipodal two-layer offset; the sole positive prism case is certified by 34 explicit geodesic witnesses covering every required pair, directly checked in verify.py. Pairwise compatibility precludes three occupied layers. The global converse routes shortest paths in unoccupied layers. Every color class gives horizontal matching-edge tokens; two parity phases and optimal injections prove the claimed chromatic number and exact partition counts. Exhaustive direct subset enumeration for eight small instances and exact-cover counts for five widths agree. Infinite statements rely on proof, not finite testing.

value.rationale: The newly introduced dual mutual-visibility coloring admits a sharp infinite-family phase transition that is not just a small graph count: C5 square K_m has nonempty dual sets but cannot be partitioned, C6 square K_m has exact chromatic number 3ceil(m/2) and a full factorial enumerator of optimal partitions, and C_n square K_m for n>=7 has no nonempty dual set. The antipodal prism compatibility and opposite matching phases explain the mechanism, while the full dual visibility polynomial offers a natural exact invariant.
